opcode_map.rs's reverse-coverage direction (real Iop_* the parse tables do NOT map) is ALREADY complete and CI-gated -- do not re-audit it by hand. vex/opcode_map_tests.rs::test_opcode_map_completeness_against_vendored_header diffs vendored_iop_names() (extracted from vendor/pyvex_ffi.h) against the parse tables and REQUIRES every unmapped name to sit in KNOWN_UNMAPPED_GROUPS with a prose reason; the sibling test_known_unmapped_groups_are_still_entirely_unmapped asserts each listed name is still both real and still unmapped, so implementing an op reddens the suite until its allowlist entry is deleted. As of angr-li4ox (2026-08-16): 1062 header names, 753 mapped, 392 allowlisted. The forward direction (dead table arms with no header declaration) is the one that needs a script.

The USEFUL work on that allowlist is re-triage, not re-audit: a group whose reason says 'not yet implemented' may be stale because the op's evaluator is already lane-generic, making the widening a parse-table entry only. Test both gates before believing it: (1) the evaluator handles the lane width/count, and (2) for any V256 shape, the evaluator's concrete fast path carries the 'if total_width <= 128' guard (invariant-concrete-bv-u128-16-byte-limit family 3). Verified carriers as of angr-li4ox: vec_int_lane.rs::vec_int_lane_op, vec_saturate.rs, vec_compare.rs, vec_shift.rs, vec_float_lane.rs, vec_lane.rs, float_cmp.rs. A lane-at-a-time evaluator with NO u128 fast path (vec_pairwise.rs::vec_rounding_avg) is safe at 256 bits for the same reason -- concat_into keeps a symbolic Concat above 128 bits.

FORWARD DIRECTION (dead arms, script method): every `*_arms!(op_str; "Iop_Prefix" => Variant { "suffix" => ... })` matches the full name prefix ++ suffix (strip_prefix + exact literal match), so a ~20-line script extracting those invocations and testing membership in vendor/pyvex_ffi.h's Iop_* set finds every dead arm in one pass (angr-0jh0j.62 removed 17 that way). The only legitimate non-header arms are the documented forward-compat placeholders And1/Or1/Xor1/PopCount8/16/32/64 -- kept because an exact-suffix arm can never misfire onto a real opcode and PopCount's evaluator (popcount_into) + tests already exist, so deleting the parse arm would strand a working impl. Trap: the *_routing tests in vex/ops/tests_*.rs and vex/ir_tests.rs assert the same copy-pasted dead strings parse, so they go red with the fix and must be corrected, not the code reverted.

DECIDING WHETHER AN OPCODE EXISTS ON THIS PIN needs two sources: (1) the IROp enum in native/angr/vendor/pyvex_ffi.h (Iop_INVALID..Iop_LAST); (2) the ppIROp name strings in .venv/.../pyvex/lib/libpyvex.so via strings, matched ANCHORED (grep -xE 'Clz(8|16|32|64)'). TRAP: an unanchored grep -oE 'Iop_Clz[0-9]+' reports Clz8/Clz16, which are prefix hits on NEON lane ops (Iop_Clz8x8 etc.) -- scalar Clz/Ctz is only 32/64. Always anchor the width or exclude the 'x' lane suffix. On the current pin: Iop_Not1 exists but And1/Or1/Xor1 do not; no scalar PopCount at any width (x86 POPCNT lifts to the gen_POPCOUNT dirty helper); ClzNat/CtzNat do not exist.

Why rustc's dead_code lint was blind in native/angr (angr-9ke6b.214, 2026-07-31): [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"] plus 23 'pub mod' declarations in lib.rs made every item externally-consumable, so dead_code reported 0 hits crate-wide while 468 unreachable_pub sites existed. Dropping rlib is impossible (benches/, examples/, tests/ and the fuzz/ cargo-fuzz project link it). The lever that works: keep rlib, but demote to 'pub(crate) mod' every top-level module no external target imports. Re-derive the keep-list with: grep -rhoE 'rustylib::[a-z_]+' native/angr/tests native/angr/benches native/angr/examples native/angr/fuzz | sort -u -- currently automaton, concretize, fuzz_api, memory, stash, state, symbolic, vex. After demoting, 'cargo clippy --fix --lib -- -W unreachable_pub' narrows the module-level items, and only THEN does dead_code fire. CRITICAL SECOND STEP: unreachable_pub does NOT lint methods inside inherent impl blocks, so 'pub fn' in 'impl Foo' stays invisible even in a pub(crate) module -- those 77 sites had to be narrowed by script, and doing so surfaced 11 MORE dead items (SegmentList::len/get_segment, PythonCallbacks::call_on_hook/call_on_syscall/call_get_register/call_put_register/get_inspect_enabled_for_debug, RustSolverContext::sym_context/from_sym_context_with_symbols). Exclude #[pymethods] impls from that pass -- PyO3 trampolines keep those live anyway. Other rustfix blind spots: items declared inside macro_rules! bodies (procedures/macros.rs, syscalls/support.rs stub_syscall!, syscalls/identity.rs constant_syscall!, interpreter/mod.rs define_execution_stats!) must be hand-edited; narrowing procedures::format_common::{parse_width_digits,parse_length_modifier,LengthModifier} breaks --features fuzzing with E0364/E0446 (they stay 'pub' with #[cfg_attr(not(feature="fuzzing"), allow(unreachable_pub))]). ALWAYS re-check dead_code under --features libvex-ffi before deleting: PythonCallbacks::call_inspect_vex_lift is dead under default features and live under libvex-ffi (which setup.py turns on). lib.rs now carries #![warn(unreachable_pub)] to keep the hole closed. Side effect to expect: clippy style lints that skip exported items (upper_case_acronyms on arch::arm::ARM / calling_conventions::ARMEABI) start firing once a module goes pub(crate).

TRAIT-METHOD BLIND SPOT (same family): rustc's dead_code lint does NOT flag unused trait methods when the trait itself is used — so a crate-interior lint sweep (angr-9ke6b.214) proves nothing about trait-method deadness. Any 'zero production callers' claim about a method on `Arch` / `CallingConvention` / any other trait must be re-derived by grep, not inferred from a clean clippy run. Worked example: Arch::register_name (angr-9ke6b.8) truly has no non-test caller and clippy --all-targets -D warnings is still clean. Decision rule when such a method turns up: (1) DELETE if it returns a hardcoded/guessed answer that would be wrong for its first real caller (precedent: CallingConvention::endness, angr-9ke6b.218 item 7); (2) DELETE if it duplicates logic that already exists elsewhere with its own tests, even when the copy is correct — the tests only pin the dead copy, so the live one can silently diverge (precedent: CallingConvention::extract_args, angr-9iny6: deleted along with its 3 tests and the MemoryUnavailable variant only it produced, because exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi is the real path and helpers_tests.rs already pins every branch); (3) KEEP + document if it is a correct computation whose only callers are load-bearing invariant tests that would lose real coverage (precedent: Arch::register_name, whose deletion would take out mod_tests::exported_register_names_reverse_resolve, ..::register_names_all_resolve_and_fit_in_u128, ..::vex_bookkeeping_fields_resolve_on_every_arch and two calling_conventions_tests sweeps; also CallingConvention::fp_arg_registers, whose per-ABI tables carry provenance FP-arg support will need).

merged_body: stat-family symlink semantics (angr-9ke6b.235, refined angr-zueuw): syscalls/file_path/stat.rs has two shared resolvers — stat_lookup_nofollow reports a FileSystem::readlink_target hit as st_mode=S_IFLNK_0777 sized to the raw target bytes, and stat_lookup_follow walks the symlink table up to MAX_SYMLINK_HOPS=8 then stats the final target; dangling link, non-UTF-8 target (targets are Vec<u8>, the known-path set is String-keyed) and cycles all return -1. Consumers: NativeLstatSyscall -> nofollow, NativeStatSyscall -> follow, NativeNewfstatatSyscall -> EITHER, selected by the AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (0x100) bit of its flag arg. That flag branch is not optional polish: ARM64's asm-generic ABI dropped legacy lstat entirely (NativeLstatSyscall is registered only on AMD64/X86/ARM/MIPS32), so glibc lstat() on aarch64 lowers to fstatat(AT_FDCWD, path, buf, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and newfstatat is the ONLY no-follow stat entry point there — any future stat-family handler that takes an AT_* flag must decide follow-vs-nofollow from it, and must treat a symbolic flag as SymbolicArgument (defer to Python) rather than assuming follow, since the two branches report different st_mode. write_stat_for_arch and all five per-arch writers take st_mode as a parameter — do NOT reintroduce a hardcoded S_IFREG_0755 inside a writer. MIPS32 is the one arch where a symlink is invisible to lstat: write_mips32_stat mirrors angr's _store_mips32, which emits NO st_mode field, so it takes _mode and only st_size differs. THE TABLE (angr-11djq.6.2): FileSystem.symlinks is Arc<HashMap<String,Vec<u8>>> (link path -> raw target bytes), populated via FileSystem::add_symlink (state/filesystem/ops.rs; also exposed to Python as a RustSimState pymethod in state/pymethods.rs), queried via readlink_target (filesystem/query.rs). readlink/readlinkat (syscalls/file_path/readlink.rs, shared write_symlink_target) write min(target_len,bufsiz) bytes with NO NUL terminator and return that count; empty table (the default) -> -1. This is a deliberate accuracy divergence from Python's stub readlink (no symlink model), sanctioned by epic 11djq.6. buf/bufsiz are read lazily only on a hit, so symbolic buf/bufsiz on a non-symlink still returns -1 with no Python fallback. serde shadow FileSystemData.symlinks is #[serde(default)] for back-compat.
